arxiv-2108-12594.title: Layer-wise Model Pruning based on Mutual Information
arxiv-2108-12594.creator: Chun Fan, Jiwei Li, Xiang Ao, Fei Wu, Yuxian Meng, Xiaofei Sun
arxiv-2108-12594.description: Abstract Inspired by mutual information (MI) based feature selection in SVMs and logistic regression, in this paper, we propose MI-based layer-wise pruning: for each layer of a multi-layer neural network, neurons with higher values of MI with respect to preserved neurons in the upper layer are preserved.

arxiv-2112-15491.title: Semantics-Recovering Decompilation through Neural Machine Translation
arxiv-2112-15491.creator: Ruigang Liang, Ying Cao, Peiwei Hu, Jinwen He, Yingjun Zhang, and Kai Chen
arxiv-2112-15491.description: Abstract Decompilation transforms low-level program languages (PL) (e.g., binary code) into high-level PLs (e.g., C/C++ ). It has been widely used when analysts perform security analysis on software (systems) whose source code is unavailable, such as vulnerability search and malware analysis.

arxiv-2210-15195.title: Masked Autoencoders Are Articulatory Learners
arxiv-2210-15195.creator: Ahmed Adel Attia, Carol Y. Espy-Wilson
arxiv-2210-15195.description: Abstract Articulatory recordings track the positions and motion of different articulators along the vocal tract and are widely used to study speech production and to develop speech technologies such as articulatory based speech synthesizers and speech inversion systems. The University of Wisconsin X-Ray Microbeam (XRMB) dataset is one of various datasets that provide articulatory recordings synced with audio recordings.

arxiv-2302-09110.title: A Novel Alternating Joint Longitudinal Model for Post-ICU Hemoglobin Prediction
arxiv-2302-09110.creator: Gabriel Demuth, Ph.D
arxiv-2302-09110.description: Abstract Anemia is common in patients post-ICU discharge. However, which patients will develop or recover from anemia remains unclear. Prediction of anemia in this population is complicated by hospital readmissions, which can have substantial impacts on hemoglobin levels due to surgery, blood transfusions, or being a proxy for severe illness.

arxiv-2404-13299.title: PCQA: A Strong Baseline for AIGC Quality Assessment Based on Prompt Condition
arxiv-2404-13299.creator: Xi Fang, Weigang Wang, Xiaoxin Lv, Jun Yan
arxiv-2404-13299.description: Abstract The development of Large Language Models (LLM) and Diffusion Models brings the boom of Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC). It is essential to build an effective quality assessment framework to provide a quantifiable evaluation of different images or videos based on the AIGC technologies. The content generated by AIGC methods is driven by the crafted prompts.

arxiv-2405-13456.title: Deep linear networks for regression are implicitly regularized towards flat minima
arxiv-2405-13456.creator: Pierre Marion, Lénaïc Chizat
arxiv-2405-13456.description: Abstract The largest eigenvalue of the Hessian, or sharpness, of neural networks is a key quantity to understand their optimization dynamics. In this paper, we study the sharpness of deep linear networks for univariate regression. Minimizers can have arbitrarily large sharpness, but not an arbitrarily small one.

arxiv-2501-01498.title: TOI-421 b: A Hot Sub-Neptune with a Haze-Free, Low Mean Molecular Weight Atmosphere
arxiv-2501-01498.creator: Brian Davenport, Eliza M.-R. Kempton, Matthew C. Nixon, Jegug Ih, Drake Deming, Guangwei Fu, E. M. May, Jacob L. Bean, Peter Gao, Leslie Rogers, Matej Malik
arxiv-2501-01498.description: Abstract Common features of sub-Neptunes atmospheres observed to date include signatures of aerosols at moderate equilibrium temperatures ( ∼ \sim 500–800 K), and a prevalence of high mean molecular weight atmospheres, perhaps indicating novel classes of planets such as water worlds. Here we present a 0.83–5 μ \mu m JWST transmission spectrum of the sub-Neptune TOI-421 b.

arxiv-2501-18669.title: The Pitfalls of “Security by Obscurity” And What They Mean for Transparent AI
arxiv-2501-18669.creator: Peter Hall, Olivia Mundahl, Sunoo Park
arxiv-2501-18669.description: Abstract Calls for transparency in AI systems are growing in number and urgency from diverse stakeholders ranging from regulators to researchers to users (with a comparative absence of companies developing AI). Notions of transparency for AI abound, each addressing distinct interests and concerns. In computer security, transparency is likewise regarded as a key concept.

arxiv-2503-02585.title: A Hypernetwork-Based Approach to KAN Representation of Audio Signals
arxiv-2503-02585.creator: Patryk Marszałek, Maciej Rut, Piotr Kawa, Piotr Syga
arxiv-2503-02585.description: Abstract Implicit neural representations (INR) have gained prominence for efficiently encoding multimedia data, yet their applications in audio signals remain limited. This study introduces the Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN), a novel architecture using learnable activation functions, as an effective INR model for audio representation. KAN demonstrates superior perceptual performance over previous INRs, achieving the lowest Log-Spectral Distance of 1.

arxiv-2505-00707.title: A high-order combined interpolation/finite element technique for evolutionary coupled groundwater-surface water problem
arxiv-2505-00707.creator: Eric Ngondiep, Areej A. Binsultan, Ibtisam M. Aldawish,
arxiv-2505-00707.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Eric Ngondiep, Areej A. Binsultan, Ibtisam M. Aldawish,. A high-order combined interpolation/finite element technique is developed for solving the coupled groundwater-surface water system that governs flows in karst aquifers. In the proposed high-order scheme we approximate the time derivative with piecewise polynomial interpolation of second-order and use the finite element discretization of piecewise polynomials of degree d and d+1 , where d\geq 2 is an integer, to approximate the space derivatives.

arxiv-2505-04488.title: “I Can See Forever!”: Evaluating Real-time VideoLLMs for Assisting Individuals with Visual Impairments Thanks: Corresponding author ( xinleihe@hkust-gz.edu.cn ).
arxiv-2505-04488.creator: Ziyi Zhang Zhen Sun Zongmin Zhang Zifan Peng Yuemeng Zhao
arxiv-2505-04488.description: Abstract The visually impaired population, especially the severely visually impaired, is currently large in scale, and daily activities pose significant challenges for them. Although many studies use large language and vision-language models to assist the blind, most focus on static content and fail to meet real-time perception needs in dynamic and complex environments, such as daily activities.

arxiv-2506-21114.title: Polynomial fingerprinting for trees and formulas
arxiv-2506-21114.creator: Mihai Prunescu
arxiv-2506-21114.description: Abstract To cater to the needs of (Zero Knowledge) proofs for (mathematical) proofs, we describe a method to transform formal sentences in 2 × 2 2\times 2 - matrices over multivariate polynomials with integer coefficients, such that usual proof-steps like modus-ponens or the substitution are easy to compute from the matrices corresponding to the terms or formulas used as arguments.

plos-pone-0008615.creator: Satyendra Kumar, Vidya A. Arankalle
plos-pone-0008615.description: PLOS ONE research article. In parts of India, Chandipura Virus (CHPV) has emerged as an encephalitis causing pathogen in both epidemic and sporadic forms. This pediatric disease follows rapid course leading to 55–75% mortality. In the absence of specific treatment, effectiveness of RNA interference (RNAi)

pmc-11295580.title: Analysis of the recombination and evolution of the new type mutant pseudorabies virus XJ5 in China
pmc-11295580.creator: Luyao Jiang, Jinlong Cheng, Hao Pan, Fan Yang, Xiemin Zhu, Jiayan Wu, Haochun Pan, Ping Yan, Jinzhu Zhou, Qingqing Gao, Changchao Huan, Song Gao
pmc-11295580.description: Pseudorabies have caused enormous economic losses in China’s pig industry and have recurred on many large pig farms since late 2011. The disease is caused by highly pathogenic, antigenic variant pseudorabies virus (vPRV) strains. Our laboratory isolated a pseudorabies virus in 2015 and named it XJ5.

pmc-11496990.title: Transport‐Friendly Microstructure in SSC‐MEA: Unveiling the SSC Ionomer‐Based Membrane Electrode Assemblies for Enhanced Fuel Cell Performance
pmc-11496990.creator: Min Li, Han Ding, Jingnan Song, Bonan Hao, Rui Zeng, Zhenyu Li, Xuefei Wu, Zachary Fink, Libo Zhou, Thomas P Russel, Feng Liu, Yongming Zhang
pmc-11496990.description: The significant role of the cathodic binder in modulating mass transport within the catalyst layer (CL) of fuel cells is essential for optimizing cell performance. This investigation focuses on enhancing the membrane electrode assembly (MEA) through the utilization of a short‐side‐chain perfluoro‐sulfonic acid (SSC‐PFSA) ionomer as the cathode binder, referred to as SSC‐MEA.

pmc-11710405.title: Clinical Recognition of Frontotemporal Dementia with Right Anterior Temporal Predominance; Recommendations of the International Working Group
pmc-11710405.creator: Hulya Ulugut
pmc-11710405.description: BackgroundAlthough frontotemporal dementia (FTD) with right anterior temporal lobe (RATL) predominance has been recognized as a separate FTD subtype, a uniform description of the syndrome is still missing. This multicenter study, led by an international working group (IWG), aims to establish a cohesive clinical phenotype and lay the groundwork for consensus on terminology and diagnostic standards.

pmc-12488576.title: Assessing the impact of enteral nutrition on peripancreatic exudate in acute pancreatitis using CT volume measurement
pmc-12488576.creator: Cui Hu, Chengcheng Tian, Chen Chen, Mengxue Huang, Jun Li, Xin Gao, Dandan Du, Jiren Wang, Lixue Zhang, Yu Wang, Mengqi Huang, Nannan Zhu, Huizhong Gan, Hao Ding, Qiao Mei
pmc-12488576.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). To investigate the effect of enteral nutrition (EN) on peripancreatic exudate in MSAP and SAP patients using CT volume measurement. This retrospective study included 328 patients diagnosed with MSAP and SAP from October 2017 to June 2023. Patients were divided into EN and non-EN groups and further stratified into acute peripancreatic fluid collection (APFC) and acute necrotic collection (ANC) groups based on local complications.

pmc-12549943.title: Detection of avermectin pesticide residues in pine trees based on magnetic Solid-Phase extraction combined technology
pmc-12549943.creator: Yi Wu, Jiaxi Ye, Yanxia Qi, Shaoyong Zhang
pmc-12549943.description: To improve the detection accuracy and efficiency of avermectin pesticide residues in pine trees, this study develops an analysis method based on MSPE combined with high-performance liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry. A core–shell magnetic nanomaterial, Fe3O4-SiO2-NH2-Schiff-TAPB-DA, is synthesized by the solvothermal method.

pmc-12604329.title: Barriers to COVID-19 vaccination and strategies to increase trust and uptake among racial and ethnic minorities with HIV in South Florida: a qualitative study
pmc-12604329.creator: Daisy Ramírez-Ortiz, Tatyana Moise, Seyedeh Yasaman Alemohammad, Mariolga Aymat, Aaliyah Gray, Michele Jean-Gilles, Diana M Sheehan, Robert Ladner, Mary Jo Trepka
pmc-12604329.description: BackgroundPeople with HIV (PWH) from racial and ethnic minority groups in the United States (US) face a high risk for severe COVID-19 outcomes and have low uptake of the COVID-19 vaccine primary series and booster doses. This study aims to provide insights into barriers and facilitators to vaccination and identify strategies to increase vaccine trust and uptake in these populations.

pmc-12988049.title: Exploring the optimal follow-up time for resectable colorectal cancer patients: a multicenter, five-year longitudinal cohort study
pmc-12988049.creator: Boyu Kang, Yihuan Qiao, Yiqian Wang, Yunlong Li, Baoliang Hu, Zecheng Zhang, Qi Wang, Jun Zhu, Jipeng Li
pmc-12988049.description: Follow-up after colorectal cancer surgery is crucial for the early detection of recurrence and metastasis. We aimed to develop a comprehensive mixed-effects model using multidimensional clinical data to explore the optimal postoperative follow-up time, thereby improving patient survival and economic benefits.

pmc-13076569.title: Reframing the paradigm: stereotactic body radiation therapy as an engineer of the tumor immune microenvironment
pmc-13076569.creator: Xuehuan Wang, Jianhua Dong, Shaojun Fang, Yao Zhou, Rui Cao, Xianshuo Cheng, Zhibin Yang
pmc-13076569.description: BackgroundStereotactic Body Radiation Therapy (SBRT) is undergoing a paradigm shift from a purely local ablative tool to a systemic immunomodulatory agent. However, a significant knowledge gap remains in understanding how to precisely “engineer” the tumor immune microenvironment (TME) to overcome resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Current approaches often rely on empirical combinations rather than biologically guided strategies.

pmc-13146244.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1716 PREDICTORS OF SUCCESSFUL REPERFUSION AND CLINICAL BENEFIT IN DISTAL MEDIUM VESSEL OCCLUSIONS
pmc-13146244.creator: Teresa Moncada Cordeiro, Miguel Serôdio, Ricardo Martins-Ascenção, Miguel Schön, Celina Poeta Do Couto, António Tavares, Mário Alcatrão, Patrícia Ferreira, Isabel Fragata, Diana Aguiar de Sousa, Ana Paiva Nunes
pmc-13146244.description: Background and aimsDistal-medium vessel occlusions (DMVO) represent 25-40% of acute ischemic strokes (AIS). Recent trials showed no benefit of endovascular therapy (EVT) over medical management in DMVO, suggesting the need for refinement of selection criteria. First-pass reperfusion (FPR) in large-vessel occlusion stroke associates with favourable outcomes. This study evaluated predictors and clinical outcomes of FPR in EVT-treated DMVO.

pmc-13280030.title: Opioid Prescription Patterns Following Medial Patellofemoral Ligament Reconstruction in Pediatric Patients: A 13-Year National Database Analysis
pmc-13280030.creator: Harmon Khela, Monty Khela, Brendan Williams
pmc-13280030.description: Background:Opioid use following surgery has been a growing concern, particularly in light of the opioid epidemic, prompting significant changes in prescribing practices. Although opioids have traditionally been a cornerstone of postoperative pain management, changing guidelines and a recent focus on opioid stewardship have likely influenced prescription patterns.

pmc-13322770.title: A rat muscle contusion model created by a modified drop-mass method using ultrasound
pmc-13322770.creator: Ryo Miyazaki, Takashi Kanamoto, Yujie Ren, Shunya Otani, Seira Sato, Tomoki Ohori, Akira Tsujii, Kosuke Ebina, Hiroyuki Tanaka, Seiji Okada, Ken Nakata
pmc-13322770.description: AimsMuscle contusion healing remains challenging because incomplete regeneration can lead to excessive scar formation, which may impair functional recovery. Therefore, reproducible animal models are important tools for investigating the healing process and evaluating potential therapeutic strategies. This study aimed to establish a reproducible muscle contusion model using a modified drop-mass method with ultrasound.

pmc-13344280.title: A caddisfly larva case–mimicked gel polymer electrolyte with high toughness and enhanced ion transport for safe lithium metal batteries
pmc-13344280.creator: Quan Liu, Xin Liang, Bing Liu, Yuan Yuan, Kang Wang, Yuxin Xia, Bingbing Li, Huakun Liu, Shixue Dou, Xiang Li, Huaxia Deng, Xinglong Gong
pmc-13344280.description: Lithium (Li) metal batteries (LMBs) promise higher energy density than Li-ion cells but face a trade-off between ionic conductivity and mechanical strength in gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs). Inspired by caddisfly larvae cases, which assemble silk with particles for toughness and permeability, we develop a caddisfly larva case–mimicked gel polymer electrolyte (CLC GPE) with high toughness and enhanced ion transport.

pmc-13367629.title: Primary High-Grade Intraperitoneal Sarcoma Mimicking a Germ Cell Tumor in an 8-Year-Old Girl in Somaliland: A Diagnostic Challenge
pmc-13367629.creator: Yahye Abdi Ali, Abdisamed Mohamoud H Ali, Mustafe Nouh Ma’alin Qasim, Khadar Jama Ibrahim
pmc-13367629.description: BackgroundPrimary intra-abdominal sarcomas in children are rare, aggressive malignancies that often present with non-specific clinical and radiological features. Differentiation from more common pediatric abdominal tumors, such as germ cell tumors, can be challenging, particularly in resource-limited settings with restricted access to advanced pathology and molecular diagnostics.

pmc-13434682.title: Psychosocial and dietary influences on eating behaviors and body mass index among geographically diverse Indian university students
pmc-13434682.creator: Girijesh Singh Mahra, Pratibha Joshi, Satyapriya, Sitaram Bishnoi, Subhashree Sahu, Sukanya Barua, Rajarshi Roy Burman
pmc-13434682.description: In the context of India’s growing youth population, the interplay of dietary habits, social influences, and psychological factors critically shapes nutritional health outcomes. This cross-sectional study examined the socio-demographic, dietary, psychological, and social determinants of eating behaviour and their association with body mass index (BMI) among 3,150 undergraduate students from agricultural universities across six Indian regions.

pmc-13561056.title: A multidimensional approach to frailty in emergency surgery for perforated peptic ulcer
pmc-13561056.creator: Muhammed Salih Süer, Serkan Demir, Ender Ergüder, Kaan Işık, Şener Balas
pmc-13561056.description: BACKGROUNDPerforated peptic ulcer (PPU) remains a high-risk surgical emergency. Although sarcopenia has been proposed as an objective surrogate of frailty, its independent prognostic value in emergency surgery is unclear. This study evaluated sarcopenia within a multidimensional frailty framework incorporating nutritional, inflammatory, and clinical parameters.METHODSThis retrospective cohort study included adult patients who underwent emergency surgery for PPU at a tertiary center.

pmc-13583096.title: Aspirin‐Derived Salicyl‐CoA Drives Histone Lysine Salicylation Regulated by CBP and SIRT2
pmc-13583096.creator: Facai Zhang, Chuanzan Zhou, Jiaoyan He, Pengpeng Huang, Rong Zhang, Huan Hu, Meng Jiao, Linyi Hu, Feng Liu, Xiaolong Qi, Xiang He, Yunkai Yang, Y Eugene Chinn, Dechao Feng, Dahong Zhang, Qi Zhang
pmc-13583096.description: Aspirin, as the most widely used drug in the world, has been reported to exert antiplatelet, anti‐inflammatory, and anti‐tumor effects. However, apart from the hydrolyzed acetyl group acetylating proteins, and salicylic acid functioning as a classic COX enzyme inhibitor, it is unknown whether the salicylic group of aspirin could participate in the salicylation of histone lysine.
